title: ADR 0025 migration left tools/data.py blind to every modifier - audit clean is meaningless and authored stat-set diversity was erased
source: wave 72 verification after the ADR 0025 corpus migration landed mid-wave
reason: ADR 0025 Accepted 2026-10-02 replaced ItemDef stub flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers with fixed_modifiers holding a master option id plus value, and a roll_spec, then migrated the corpus. 7950 of 7950 item files now carry fixed_modifiers and roll_spec and zero carry the old maps. Three consequences. First, the gate is blind - tools/data.py line 44 still declares dicts as flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers only, and every audit and distribution rule reads those two keys, so the audit sees zero modifiers corpus-wide and reports data audit clean while validating nothing, and tools data distribution prints Modifier Stat Distribution none plus 34 declared stats never used by any item, which is false since it is all 34. A clean audit is no longer evidence of anything. Second, authored diversity was destroyed rather than migrated - a wave-72 five-stat item authored as breakthrough_chance plus evasion plus fortune plus penetration plus physique at three-decimal percents now reads fixed_modifiers with a single base_comprehension option at integer value 6 and roll_spec count 1, so the stat-combination and modifier-value diversity built across waves 69 to 72, including 100 percent stat-pair coverage, 142 distinct three-stat sets and 81 distinct percent values, is no longer present in the data. Third, tools/data.py still emits the dead schema, since _new_command writes percent_modifiers and flat_modifiers, so any item created with data new --percent lands in the legacy shape while the corpus is in the new one. HEAD item_def.gd still accepts both shapes through build_fixed_modifiers, which is why 4849 of 4890 tests pass. tools/item_migrate.py, the tool that rewrote all 7950 files, is still untracked.
next: Do not dispatch item-generation agents until tools/data.py is taught the ADR 0025 schema: add fixed_modifiers and roll_spec to the parsed dicts, rewrite every modifier rule to read them, and either teach _new_command to emit fixed_modifiers and roll_spec or document that new items are still authored in the legacy shape. Until then do not cite data audit clean as evidence, and treat the tools data distribution modifier sections as non-functional. Separately decide whether the authored stat-set programme is retired under ADR 0025 - if it is, waves 69 to 72 need a target expressed in option-pool membership, roll budget and rarity/realm pairing rather than authored stat combinations.

title: ADR 0025 catalog eligibility is category-scoped and far too narrow - 99.4 percent of authored stat diversity was silently discarded on migration
source: wave 72 survival measurement against the ADR 0025 catalog
reason: ADR 0025 replaces authored stat maps with master-catalog option references, and the catalog is far narrower than the stat vocabulary the corpus uses, so authored diversity is discarded rather than migrated. Measured over wave 72 own 344 non-material items: of 501 stat tokens encoded in their ids, only 3 survive as fixed_modifiers options, a 0.6 percent survival rate. Per item, 242 lost every authored stat, 101 lost some, and 1 kept all. The cause is category-scoped eligibility. The catalog holds 107 options over 92 stats, but eligibility is narrow and unequal: equipment gets 93 options over 92 stats, technique gets 36, material gets 5, and consumable gets only 9 - awareness, body_integrity, desire, essence, health, mind_power, qi, stamina and tribulation_essence. Those 9 consumable options are resource pools, not combat stats, so a consumable item can no longer carry a combat modifier at all. Every one of the 184 consumable items in this wave now grants health via the restore_health category default instead of its authored effect. tools/item_migrate.py drops any stat whose option is ineligible or missing with no warning, and then substitutes CATEGORY_FIXED, so the loss is silent.
next: Decide the programme target before another wave. Authored stat-combination diversity is void under ADR 0025: pair coverage, three and four and five stat sets, and novel modifier values cannot survive migration for consumable items and mostly cannot for technique items. The expressible axes are now option-pool membership, roll budget where count comes from rarity via RARITY_COUNT common 1 magic 2 rare 3 legendary 4, rarity and realm pairing, and category eligibility coverage. Two things need an owner decision. First, whether consumable items are meant to carry combat stats at all, since the current catalog says they cannot and the corpus says they always did. Second, whether the catalog should be widened so technique and consumable have real option coverage. Until that is settled, target equipment only, where all 92 stats are eligible. Separately, tools/data.py still parses only flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers, so data audit and data distribution cannot see any modifier and a clean audit is not evidence.

title: tools/item_migrate.py is broken and untracked - missing import zlib makes the only sanctioned ADR 0025 migration path unrunnable
source: wave 73 end-to-end schema probe in an isolated temp root
reason: tools/item_migrate.py is the only sanctioned path from authored stat maps to ADR 0025 option references, and it cannot run. Line 164 calls zlib.crc32 inside realm_for, but the module imports only re, pathlib.Path and two local modules - there is no import zlib anywhere in the file. Every run dies on the first item with NameError: name zlib is not defined, confirmed against an isolated temp root and against the real corpus with --limit 1. The file is also untracked with no git history at all, so the migration that rewrote all 7950 item files cannot be reproduced from anything in the repository and the working state of the tool is unknown. Consequence: nobody can author new-schema content, and nobody can re-run or verify the corpus migration.
next: Add import zlib to tools/item_migrate.py - that single line is the whole fix, and the tool then runs in dry-run by default so it is safe to validate before --apply. Then commit the tool, because until it is tracked the corpus migration is unreproducible. After that, verify the migration is faithful by re-running it in dry run and confirming it reports zero changes, which also proves the 7950 already-migrated files are stable under it. Only then re-target generation, per DEF-0048.

reason: VERIFIED. tribulation_ok requires tribulation.survived(), which is only set by apply_result(success=true) - and apply_result has NO once-guard (core/tribulation.gd:113). So resolving a fight pays _apply_rewards once, then the breakthrough pays it again at body/advancement.gd:147 and :203, qi/advancement.gd:120, qi/breakthrough_transaction.gd:140 and mind/advancement.gd:322. reason: tools/data.py:545-547 sets root_types to every known source type except craft, which makes boss: and domain: roots regardless of whether any runtime can produce them. _unobtainable therefore returns empty and the audit reports clean while no boss spawn or loot runtime exists. title: Scaled attack and defense stats have no reader, so the 551x ladder is unobservable
reason: RealmScaling.apply has one production caller (core/breakthrough.gd:46) and lands on seven MULT modifiers including ATTACK_PHYSICAL, DEFENSE_SPIRITUAL, DEFENSE_PHYSICAL. No code reads those four attack/defense ids outside their own derivation in actor_stats.gd:152-159, and modules/combat/api.gd exposes only a shield that absorbs externally-computed damage. title: Technique system: codex, slots and mastery
reason: The three cultivation paths, the 30-realm ladder and the learned-but-unreachable combat stats all exist, but there is no way to acquire, hold, equip or use a technique. ADR 0053 fixes the three-state model (item delivers, codex holds, slot binds), ADR 0054 fixes passive delivery as namespaced StatModifiers, ADR 0055 fixes the magnitude ladder, ADR 0056 fixes ownership. This entry is the parent of the technique work and carries no implementation of its own.

title: Author TechniqueDef: the schema for a learnable art
reason: A technique has no content type. ADR 0056 settles the layer (module-owned Resource, per the 25-of-30 precedent), but no field list exists. The genre reference supplies the required axes: grade, active-or-passive, element, school, meridian or acupoint gate, qi cost, cooldown, mastery ceiling, and whether the parents are consumed on fusion. None can be invented later without reauthoring every technique.

title: Learn a technique: codex entry, path gate and learning cost
reason: ItemUse._apply_learned grants flat base attributes once and discards the item, so all 1363 technique items are interchangeable stat sticks. ADR 0053 requires study to produce a permanent, path-gated CodexEntry instead. The learning cost needs a per-realm ladder whose step stays at or below the authored work budget, or technique study becomes the cheapest power in the game.
next: Implement study consuming the item into a CodexEntry, gate on the technique's own path rank rather than the best path, and size the learning ladder to the measured 1.035714 floor.

title: Three cultivation seeds have drifted from their generators
reason: Because the generators skip existing files, the authored .tres seeds no longer match the code that supposedly defines them. qi.progress_required is authored as 100*max(1,R-1) but seed_systems.py emits 100*max(1,i)^1.45; qi.comprehension_required is authored as 10+2*max(1,i) but the generator emits 10+6i+2i^2; body.work_required corresponds to a power table of roughly 4329x, not the authored 551.46x. A fresh checkout regenerating any of these changes every step ratio, which is exactly what DEF-0083 sizes its ladder against.
next: Reconcile generator and data, then pin the step ratios with a test so the work-budget floor in ADR 0055 cannot silently move.

title: Equip techniques into path-typed slots
reason: ADR 0053 requires per-path slot counts plus universal slots growing with realm tier, so a loadout is a statement about which path is being bet on. The genre convention is four active slots and a known set far larger than that; the gap between known and equipped is the design space. Nothing in the repo expresses a slot limit today.
next: Implement equip/unequip against the codex, with slot counts read from each path's published configuration and universal slots keyed off realm tier.

title: Deliver passive techniques as namespaced StatModifiers
reason: ADR 0054 settles the mechanism. The audit confirmed the cost is about 110 lines in one new file with no change to ActorStats, Equipment or the modifier pipeline, because ItemEffects.stat_modifiers is already a static module-agnostic facade used by sockets and set bonuses. The source tag must be technique:<id> so it cannot collide with the &"realm" tag or an instance id.
next: Copy the SocketEffects.apply shape for rebuild, and wire a settle loop that suspends a technique whose upkeep it cannot pay without unequipping it.

title: ItemRequirement resolves realm to the best path, so path-scoped gates cannot reuse it
reason: item_requirement.gd:140-151 deliberately takes the highest realm ordinal across every cultivation path, documented as so an item never demands one specific system. A qi technique must be gated on the qi rank alone, so the existing scalar min_realm_index cannot express the requirement. This is the only genuinely unavoidable change to a shared item type that the technique system forces.
next: Add a path-scoped ordinal alongside min_realm_index, or gate in the technique module's own validator and leave ItemRequirement untouched.

title: Equipment.rebuild ignores suspension, so rebuilding a suspended slot reactivates it
reason: equipment.gd effects(slot) returns an empty array for a suspended slot, but rebuild() at line 109 reads ItemEffects.resolve directly and would re-add a suspended item's modifiers. The consequence today is latent because nothing in src/ calls settle; it becomes real the moment a tick scheduler drives upkeep. The technique system needs the same pattern to be correct.
next: Add the is_suspended check to rebuild() and pin it with a test that a suspended slot survives a rebuild.

title: Mastery: a per-technique ladder that scales power, cost and cooldown together
reason: ADR 0053 separates the hold gate from the strength gate so realm alone never makes a technique strong. Without mastery, a later technique is a strict numeric upgrade and every build collapses into whatever dropped most recently. The genre convention is five rungs each multiplying power up and cost and cooldown down, which keeps an old technique economically competitive.
next: Add a mastery track per codex entry accruing only on activations that actually fired, and require a second resource (a second copy of the manual) for the top rung.

title: Active techniques are blocked on a damage pipeline that does not exist
reason: The blocker is GONE. A combat_engine module now exists (11 files: spine.gd, damage.gd, duel.gd, exchange.gd, band.gd, recoil.gd, status_apply.gd, qi_damage.gd, combat_tuning.gd, mechanism_slot.gd, api.gd) and it already consumes TechniqueDef: CombatSpine.base_damage(attacker, technique) at spine.gd:184 reads technique.magnitude through RealmRate.factor(actor.realm()), and CombatEngineApi.resolve_hit is its public entry. Active technique execution was implemented on top of it (DEF-0125), composing through a resolver Callable bound in app/ rather than an undeclared module dependency. DEF-0078 and DEF-0007 are effectively answered by combat_engine, so this entry can close.
next: After DEF-0078 and DEF-0007, define resolve_attack(attacker, defender, technique) as the one contract the active path needs, and resolve BL-0114 first so crit has a single source.

title: The 1363 technique items are seeding filler and cannot carry technique identity
reason: tools/item_migrate.py reproduces every field of every technique .tres: 100% of files use the same 10 fields with zero variance, ids are template concatenations of stat names, display_name is the id title-cased, 61.8% carry a craft:* source, and about 50% of option_id occurrences use options the pool marks equipment-only. Meanwhile the roughly 25 technique-legal cult_* options, including cult_technique_power and cult_technique_cost_reduction, are used by nothing. No technique has a unique stat, mechanic, combo or scaling rule, so there is no signal for a player choosing between manuals.
next: Keep the corpus as an acquisition vector, but author real techniques separately with distinct payloads; retire the equipment-only option_ids from technique items and activate the cult_* pool.

title: tools arch cannot see a class's base type or bare refs outside ui/
reason: enforce.py never inspects what a class extends, and rules.py documents that bare typed references are unresolved with scan_bare enabled only for ui/. That is how contracts/skill_def.gd (a Resource in contracts) and app/skill_system.gd (a feature system in the composition root) passed the gate. registry.json is a permission list, not an inventory: a module listed in UI_MODULES but absent on disk passes silently, so the green arch run says nothing about whether a module has a body.
next: Flag a Resource subclass in contracts/ and a stateful system in app/ as warnings, and report registered-but-absent modules explicitly.

title: Technique codex and loadout screens
reason: A permanent unbounded codex and a small path-typed slot set are two different screens with two different questions, and neither is expressible against today's item panel. Both are pure consumers per the split dev cycle: gameplay publishes preview() and the slot state, ui renders it.

title: Nothing in the codebase damages a health pool, and a Damageable class would be ceremony
reason: No code subtracts health. The only negative pool changes are shield.gd:23, body_cultivation/advancement.gd:125,183 (integrity) and the orphaned skill_system/input_handler. loot_state.gd:196 subtracts from a plain Dictionary of a boss encounter driven by a hardcoded 25.0 UI constant, so it is not an actor and not a stat consumer. ResourcePool at contracts/resource_pool.gd:28-31 already has current, change() clamping at 0 and a changed signal, and Actor.resource(&health) is sized from MAX_HEALTH, so it already is the damageable shape.

title: DEF-0078, DEF-0007 and DEF-0090 form a dependency cycle, so the recorded order is not a sequence
reason: DEF-0090 depends_on DEF-0078 and DEF-0007, but DEF-0078's own next field is to build the combat resolution that consumes the scaled stats, which is DEF-0090's deliverable, and DEF-0007's next is the same damage pipeline. So DEF-0090 is blocked by an item that is blocked by it. Also combat has zero test coverage: game/tests/modules/combat/ does not exist while game/tests/modules/elements/ holds 7 files, so even Shield is untested.
next: Merge DEF-0078, DEF-0007 and DEF-0090 into one work item and rewrite the chain as: resolve the crit decision, add elements to combat's deps, then write resolve_attack once, which closes all three.

title: resolve_attack contract: additive defense is mandatory, and BL-0114's duplicate-crit premise is wrong
reason: Crit ids are not duplicates: Stat.CRIT_CHANCE is crit_chance (stat.gd:36) and MindStats.CRITICAL_CHANCE is critical_chance (mind_cultivation/stats.gd:14), so they cannot collide in _provider_cache. Core wins because it is in RATE_STATS (stat.gd:77) and authored content already writes core_crit_chance, while no authored data uses the mind twins. Signature: CombatApi.resolve_attack(attacker, defender, technique: Dictionary, rng) -> Dictionary, with technique a plain dict so DEF-0082 is not a blocker. Formula: attack from ATTACK_PHYSICAL or ATTACK_SPIRITUAL by damage_type plus element power; defense = max(0, defender defense - penetration); mitigated = attack * (100/(100+defense)); element multiplier from ElementsApi.multiplier; crit on core CRIT_CHANCE clamped to 0.75; damage = mitigated * resisted * crit * (1 - DAMAGE_REDUCTION).
next: Use the K/(K+defense) additive form, never attack/defense: a ratio divides 551.46 by 551.46 and makes the realm ladder permanently invisible, which is the mechanism behind DEF-0078. Add elements to combat's deps in registry.json before writing it.

title: Salvage plan for the 622-line orphaned prototype, including a dead combo multiplier
reason: Verified orphan: no .tscn, no app/main.gd and no script references skill_def, skill_system, input_handler, consumable_system or player_adapter; their only consumer is tests/app/test_input_system.gd. Keep in skill_def.gd: combat_only gate, effect_radius/is_area, is_action_skill, two-pool cost. Delete effect_type and effect_value, because one float cannot express element, penetration or crit, which is exactly why use_skill returns a descriptor nobody consumes. Delete to_dict/from_dict. Keep in skill_system.gd: cooldown array and tick, cooldown_ratio, the effective-cooldown COOLDOWN_REDUCTION read, and the afford/pay pair. Delete _save/_load, which persists skill.to_dict() where consumable_system persists String(def_id), and delete set_combat_state/is_in_combat. Delete COMBO_PATTERNS from input_handler.gd: multiplier 1.5 is asserted to exist at test_input_system.gd:224 and read by nothing.
next: Apply the salvage, delete the two duplicate combat state machines (PlayerAdapter.State and InputHandler._in_combat) in favour of one CombatApi-owned component, and keep consumable_system.gd verbatim as the id-persistence model while moving it out of app/.

title: OPEN: a dual-path technique requires both paths at the gate, or is an either/or commitment
reason: ADR 0059 decides the both-paths reading: requiring both makes a second path a second investment and keeps the dual build's slot cost real, at the price of a smaller audience. The rejected alternative is an either/or commitment, where satisfying one path at the floor admits the technique and the other path stays free, which would make dual-cultivation strictly better than a single path. Nothing in the repo settles which is right: modules/dual_cultivation and modules/fertility already scope their content to a dual audience but neither requires two cultivation paths, and AGENTS.md requires fertility content to stay clinical and mechanical, so neither module can be the evidence. A human may reasonably prefer either/or, which is the genre's usual reading.
next: If overruled, ADR 0059 is superseded by a new ADR and min_path_realm gains an either/or mode: a DUAL gate passes when any named path meets its floor. Pin whichever reading is chosen with a contract test on ItemRequirement.unmet.

title: Fertility cult_* options are equipment-only, so no technique can carry them
reason: ADR 0054's passive option pool is the technique-legal slice of master_option_pool.jsonl. cult_conception_chance, cult_gestation_speed and cult_maternal_resilience are marked categories [equipment] only, while cult_fertility, cult_charm, cult_purity, cult_dual_cultivation_rate, cult_essence_capacity and cult_essence_regen are technique-legal. That split is correct today and should stay: a technique is permanent and path-gated, so a fertility technique would be an irreversible acquisition of a pregnancy-affecting bonus from a manual, which is a different consent model than wearing a belt. AGENTS.md additionally requires all fertility content to stay clinical and mechanical.
next: Keep the split. If a dual_cultivation technique ever needs a fertility-family bonus beyond the six technique-legal ids, widen the category deliberately in the pool rather than authoring an ineligible option, and keep the wording clinical.

title: QiStats.TECHNIQUE_POWER and TECHNIQUE_COST_REDUCTION are provider-only and have no modifier reader
reason: QiProvider.contribute emits both ids as derived stats and nothing in src/ reads them; the technique system would be their first consumer. They are also not in Stat.RATE_STATS, and they are the pool's cult_technique_power and cult_technique_cost_reduction options, so a passive technique that grants them and an active technique that reads them have to agree on one resolution order or the same stat gets counted twice.

title: Quest completion grants fate: shipped 2026-10-03 in QuestApi._complete via QuestGrants.pay

title: No clock or world-turn seam exists, so fate cannot accrue over calendar time
reason: If a fate ever needs to accrue over time - a counter that rises per day survived, a destiny that unlocks after a season - nothing in this repo can drive it. There is no clock, no calendar, no world turn and no tick that advances time; the only ticks are per-frame physics. DestinyApi.record() is the accrual verb and it takes an explicit amount from a caller, so a time-based earn needs a time source that does not exist.
next: RESOLVED 2026-10-03 by build/sect_nation_clock_research.md. The premise behind the original entry was stale: app/ ALREADY owns the single frame driver (app/item_workbench_app.gd:98 _process(delta), passed down an explicit wire through app/status_loop.gd:56), and a test pins the tree to exactly three frame drivers. There is no calendar and no period, which is the part that was true. BL-0198 therefore needs a PERIOD ACCUMULATOR hung off the existing tick, not new time infrastructure - and it must add ZERO new frame drivers, because a fourth _process fails game/tests/app/test_status_clock.gd:222-230. Correct the stale reason text on this entry when convenient.

title: A consume/clear fate affordance contradicts ADR 0065 and is refused here on purpose
reason: Recorded so a future agent finds the decision instead of re-litigating it. ADR 0065 states the invariant plainly: fate is earned, never chosen, never equipped and never removed. There is no revoke path in the module - not for a penalty, not for a reset, not for a debug tool - and DestinyProjection.strip() exists only so apply() can rebuild, never to be called by gameplay. normalize() may drop an entry only when it is unreadable or names content the catalog no longer ships, never because the player did something.

title: A scheduled/timed domain opening needs a world clock that does not exist, and wall-clock time in save state is already a recorded defect
reason: A secret realm that opens on a cycle is a core genre idiom and it is blocked on an enablement, not merely unbuilt: the repo has no calendar, no world turn and no tick that advances time. The only time reads are Time.get_ticks_msec in input_handler and get_ticks_usec in socket_forge_program, and body_cultivation/attempt.gd:54 records that naming an attempt with wall-clock time made it a DIFFERENT attempt after every reload. A grace-period timer persisted into module_data and keyed on wall-clock time is that same defect one level up. If an opening cycle ships, the timer must be an absolute tick counter decremented by the same delta that ticks StatusEffect.remaining, exactly how ADR 0075's zones already age.

reason: BL-0049, the no-rng constraint. EconomyApi.purse already answers wealth because the numeraire prices at exactly 1. ceiling = purse * appetite_percent / 100, where appetite is an authored tag table on Actor.tags (ADR 0074), so the decision needs no rng and no npc or sect dependency. Rare goods attract deep purses as ARITHMETIC, not as an emergent roll: a legendary lot is 4x a common one through RARITY_WEIGHT, so only a deep purse clears its opening.

title: a captive is a custody claim, never a tradeable thing
reason: The brief asks for captured actors and mobs to trade. ADR 0094 already refuses it by construction: an Actor has no ItemDef, so base_worth is 0 and exchange hits no_settlement, writing nothing. Making it tradeable needs either a captive ItemDef, which would put a person through RARITY_WEIGHT and RealmRate and assign them a market price, or a second leg type, which is the and-rule and the ADR 0066 failure. The representation is an InstitutionClaim obligation line: transferred moves the claim and settles the old holder's line; released maps to NpcPresence.RETIRED, already terminal. Blocked on three prerequisites, each on another module: Actor.to_dict omits statuses, so a restored captive comes back with full health; an institution cannot hold a claim because SectState lives in the player's module_data (DEF-0119); and NpcPresence has no custody state. Recommend naming an NpcDef id and never an Actor, so the live actor is minted on demand.

THE PRESCRIBED FIX IS WRONG: swapping the two assignments in _spend does not work, because _absorb returned 0.0 for two different facts - no shield bound, and the shield took it all - so one number carried two opposite meanings and no arrangement of the two assignments is right for both cases. Measured: the 1553-of-7982 shortfall is attributed entirely to two unshipped kinds. blocking signatures over 6429 orphans: gather-only 821, quest-only 1392, gather+quest 4150, unattributed 66. NO boss or domain source blocks anything: all 331 boss defs are hosted by one of 160 authored LootEncounterDefs, all 160 domains have an encounter, 0 unhosted droppers. Simulating gather as shipped moves 1553 -> 6591 reachable (+5038, +82%); simulating quest as shipped moves it 1553 -> 7078; both -> 7981 (the entire corpus). gather is the cheaper half. It is also the one with NO substrate: game/data/holdings/nodes/ does not exist (0 authored ResourceNodeDefs), and the holdings module is forbidden by design from turning yield into items - 'A node pays a ledger line, never items' (resource_node_def.gd:15), 'Yield is a ledger line, never items' (holdings/api.gd:21-24), BL-0191. So gather needs a NEW forager subsystem with an items edge, not a wiring fix. quest is the opposite: the module SHIPS (QuestApi/QuestGrants/QuestCatalog/BeatDirector), but QuestGrants.pay records item grants as unspent with reason no_inventory_dependency (quest_grants.gd:71-73) because quest declares no items dependency, and all 442 authored quest: ids are dangling (0 resolve) against 5 real QuestDefs.
next: Decide, per source kind, then act on gather first. (1) Add a forager module that turns a world object into an inventory item - ItemsApi edge declared, node defs authored under game/data/holdings/nodes/ or a new dir - and ship it by flipping KIND_GATHER shipped:false -> true in item_sources.gd:89 AND adding the matching Route to RUNTIME_ROUTES in tools/data.py:217; the two-sided cross-check at tools/data.py:878 (_route_agreement_problems) will fail if only one is flipped. (2) Separately and cheaply: give quest an items edge so QuestGrants.pay's GRANT_ITEM branch (quest_grants.gd:71) calls ItemsApi instead of recording no_inventory_dependency - that alone is 1392 items. (3) Only then re-point the 442 dangling quest: refs - either author 442 QuestDefs or rewrite them bare 'quest' (1379 items already use the bare form). Do NOT re-author 160 encounters or 331 boss defs: they are already complete and verified hosted. Do NOT delete the ~5000 gather/quest items: all 7981 are graph-obtainable and the corpus is one recipe closure away from fully reachable.

title: NpcApi.spawn returns a RefCounted Actor; WorldEntry.spawn_npc wants a Node2D
reason: Type-incompatible and unbridged. NpcApi.spawn (modules/npc/api.gd) mints an engine-agnostic Actor, which deliberately has no scene-tree presence (ADR 0001), while WorldEntry.spawn_npc (app/world_entry.gd) calls add_child on a Node2D. No scene extends WorldEntry today, so the two never meet -- but any future world scene with real npc markers cannot be stocked from the npc module without a bridge. A fake Node2D wrapper is NOT acceptable: it would mint a second identity no other system can see, so NpcRegistry, NpcApi.presence_here and WorldSpawn-derived interactable rows would all disagree about who is in the room. WorldStage.register_npc(actor) deliberately takes the Actor the caller already has instead of pretending to bridge.
next: Decide one: (a) a Body/Sprite2D view node owned by app/, registered with NpcRegistry as a presentation of an existing Actor, so one Actor has one identity and two representations; or (b) author real npc scenes and have ActorFactory return a Node-wrapped Actor. Whichever is chosen, it needs an ADR and a registry entry -- do not add an app/ -> npc import in the meantime.

title: EventApi.begin now has a production caller; EventApi.advance still does not, because no caller owns a PERIOD
reason: Half of ADR 0117 line 85 is closed and half is not. EventApi had zero production callers, so no module owned the moment ADR 0114 requires. The attach half is now wired at item_workbench_app.gd:233 (EventApi.attach, the NpcBoot.install precedent: one attach line, on the line that already calls NpcBoot.install, after DestinyApi.attach so a fate grant has a ledger to land in). The ADVANCE half cannot be wired honestly yet: EventApi.advance(actor, periods) carries NO default and refuses periods <= 0 by design (ADR 0085 pull-based tick, DEF-0111), and NOTHING in production owns a PERIOD COUNT. StatusLoop passes a float delta of seconds to StatusApi.tick_statuses; there is no month/week/world-turn caller anywhere in game/src, and app/ is forbidden from inventing one (tools/arch/rules.py app-state rule). Converting seconds to periods would be the timer ADR 0085 refuses. So EventApi.advance stays at zero production callers by decision, not by oversight.
next: Name the owner of the world's period counter first (a turn/season/cycle concept above the monthly clock), then give that owner exactly one call to EventApi.advance(actor, periods) and assert with a test that two pulls with no elapsed period resolve nothing extra - the property test_event.gd already proves of the facade, which is why the wiring needs no new test of its own.

title: OPEN: a technique manual raises core attributes through ItemUse._apply_learned, bypassing every gate
reason: items/item_use.gd:63-71 grants FLAT base attributes via actor.stats.set_base for any ItemDef routed to LEARNED, completely un-gated. The worry that this BYPASSES the technique gate was checked and REFUTED: ItemDef (item_def.gd:9-34) exports no technique_id and no grant payload, TechniqueCodex.record is the single insertion primitive, and TechniquesApi.learn is the only path that can create a codex entry - and it is gated. But the defect stands on its own: set_base bypasses the modifier stack, cannot be stripped or rebuilt idempotently, and DOES satisfy get_base, which is exactly what ADR 0052/0054 pinned against (a technique can never satisfy its own requirement with the stats it grants). A manual therefore feeds straight through ItemRequirement base-allocation checks.
next: Replace the set_base grant in _apply_learned with a modifier through actor.stats.add_modifier (PERCENT on rate stats, never FLAT), source-tagged, so it can be stripped and re-derived. Needs its own ADR: it changes a shared items behaviour authored content already depends on, and ADR 0056 forbids growing that facade past its cap. Until then a sect library gate is NOT bypassed, so BL-0189 is UNBLOCKED and can proceed.

title: OPEN: SocialState.regard is declared, persisted, read and written by NOTHING
reason: social/social_state.gd:27 declares regard, :83 and :91-92 persist and restore it, and social/api.gd:157 publishes it through summary(). An exhaustive grep of game/src/ for regard|reputation|REPUTATION found no writer outside the state class itself. So the read model ADR 0091 promised is present and permanently empty: every institution a player joins contributes nothing to regard, and the sect/nation feature (BL-0200) has no way to record that a player is known to an institution. SocialApi is at 10 of 12 methods, so the writer fits without splitting the facade.
next: Add one SocialApi verb that writes regard through apply_cause (or a sibling using the same authored-cause discipline), and have sect/nation membership and notable deeds move it rather than keeping a second number. Standing is what an institution thinks of you; regard is what everyone else does, and ADR 0064's whole point is that those differ.
